title: Mixed-ligand Fe( iii ) and Cu( ii ) complexes of sulfasalazine and 2,6-di(1-pyrazolyl)pyridine: synthesis, comprehensive characterization, DFT, molecular docking and biological studies
content: Two novel mixed-ligand Fe(iii) and Cu(ii) complexes, FeDPSU and CuDPSU were prepared from sulfasalazine (SU) and 2,6-di(1-pyrazolyl)pyridine (DP) and characterized by elemental analysis, molar conductivity, FT-IR, UV-Vis spectroscopy, magnetic susceptibility, mass spectrometry, Job's method and TG/DrTG analysis. The complexes were obtained in good yields (80 and 84% respectively) and exhibited low molar conductivities (11.08 and 10.86 Ω−1 cm2 mol−1), indicating non-electrolytic behavior. Elemental analysis, and Job's method, supported a 1 : 1 : 1 metal : DP : SU stoichiometry. FT-IR data suggested coordination of SU through phenolate and carboxylate oxygen atoms and DP through its three nitrogen donor atoms. The complexes are characterized by a distorted octahedral environment around the metal centers. The magnetic moments were 1.92 and 1.79 BM for FeDPSU and CuDPSU respectively. Ligand-field bands were found at 490 and 585 nm respectively. From TG/DrTG analysis there is no lattice water in both complexes; there is no coordinated water in FeDPSU and one coordinated water molecule in CuDPSU. The maximum stability of both complexes in solution was observed at pH 6–8. The DFT calculations show that the electronic properties change significantly upon complexation. The HOMO–LUMO gaps were reduced from 3.37 eV for SU and 3.49 eV for DP to 2.50 eV for FeDPSU and 2.27 eV for CuDPSU. CuDPSU also exhibited the lowest hardness (1.13 eV), maximum softness (0.88 eV), and maximum nucleophilicity index (3.50). Biological testing determined that the antimicrobial activity significantly increased after the complexation. CuDPSU exhibited inhibition zones of 28–33 mm against tested bacteria and 22 and 19 mm against Candida albicans and Aspergillus niger respectively. Its MIC values were as low as 30 µM and its antibacterial and antifungal activity indexes were up to 100% and 95%, respectively. Furthermore, the anti-inflammatory activity was enhanced upon complexation with IC50 values of 81.67 µM for FeDPSU and 75.86 µM for CuDPSU in comparison to 115.62 and 124.08 µM for SU and DP, respectively. Molecular docking also gave information about the interaction profiles. The binding energies of FeDPSU and CuDPSU were −8.40 and −8.70 kcal mol−1 respectively, against E. coli DNA gyrase B (1KZN) while SU and DP showed −7.20 and −6.90 kcal mol−1 respectively. For COX-2 (6COX) the corresponding values were −8.30 and −8.80 kcal mol−1 for the complexes and −7.60 and −6.50 kcal mol−1 for the free ligands. The docking validation showed the RMSD values of the re-docked native ligands were 1.107 Å and 1.114 Å. Overall, the experimental and computational results indicate that coordination of SU and DP with Fe(iii) and Cu(ii) greatly alters their structural, electronic and biological properties, with CuDPSU showing especially strong antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory responses under the investigated conditions.
